text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.3% today to $137.30, bouncing back after a rough two weeks that saw the stock drop nearly 8%. The recovery came as oil prices stabilized: US crude held steady around $99.64 per barrel, while Brent (the international benchmark) steadied after dipping below $90 last week on reports that the Iran conflict might be winding down. The stock had been pressured by those hopes for lower oil prices, which reduce energy company profits, but today's modest gain suggests some of that selling may have run its course.

The stock remains down significantly over the past fortnight, caught between two crosscurrents: lower geopolitical risk from potential de-escalation with Iran would mean cheaper oil long-term, but that's the opposite of what oil producers want to see. With crude still well above $99, investors appear to be taking a wait-and-see stance rather than betting heavily on a major oil price collapse.
